newsitem.title: CHINA: China drug crackdown nets 55,211, drive extended.
newsitem.headline: China drug crackdown nets 55,211, drive extended.

text.p: China has arrested 55,211 people and seized 1,623 kg (3,570 lbs) of heroin since the start of a crackdown on drugs in April and officials said the problem was spreading, the China Women's News said on Monday.
To try to combat the drugs problem, the crackdown that had been scheduled to end in September had been extended to the end of the year, the newspaper said.
Police cracked 39,015 cases between mid-April and the end of July, smashing 499 drug rings and 1,196 underground markets, and obtaining 2,888 confessions, it said.

Law enforcement officials confiscated 20,000 tablets of Ecstasy, and 400 kg (880 lbs) of methamphetamine hydrochloride, or "ice", in addition to 1,623 kg of heroin, and destroyed about 100 tonnes of chemicals used in drugs processing, it said.
Authorities had arrested 55,211 suspects and set up 187 additional forced rehabilitation centres and entered 30,000 addicts into such programmes in the three-month period, it said.
However, the drug problem showed no sign of diminishing despite the crackdown, which has been accompanied by a string of executions of traffickers, it said.

"Although the results of the battle against drugs is encouraging, the seriousness of the problem is more clearly exposed as the struggle intensifies, allowing us no room for optimism," the newspaper said, quoting a report by a committee set up to tackle the drugs problem.

Narcotics were being smuggled into China through proliferating channels, and new drugs were spreading rapidly, with Ecstasy showing up in 17 cities and provinces soon after it was introduced to China, the report said.
Drug use in China was nearly wiped out under strict communist controls but has surged in recent years as two decades of economic reform have eroded the state's power over people's lives.
China had 520,000 registered addicts in 1995, soaring from 148,000 in 1991, state media has said. Officials and analysts say the real number of people hooked on drugs is much higher.
